title: Enoxaparin (Lovenox)

uses.doseText: 40 mg SC daily; CrCl <30: 30 mg SC daily
notes: Timing after ICH/IVT: see VTE prophylaxis entry (pending)

uses.doseText: 1 mg/kg SC q12h (or 1.5 mg/kg daily); CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg daily
notes: CVT and pregnancy: LMWH is the preferred parenteral agent (Saposnik 2024)

renalHepatic: CrCl <30: reduce dose (above) — accumulates; consider UFH (label)

timing.halfLifeText: ~4.5 h after a single dose; ~7 h after repeated dosing (anti-Xa) (label)
holdBeforeProcedure: Neuraxial/LP: ≥12 h after a prophylactic dose; ≥24 h after a treatment dose (label)
Next dose ≥4 h after catheter removal (label)
CrCl <30: consider roughly doubling these intervals (label)
thrombolysisRule: Full treatment-dose LMWH within 24 h: no IVT (Powers 2019: COR III: Harm, B-NR; not restated in AHA 2026). Prophylactic doses excluded

reversal.doseText: <8 h since dose: 1 mg per 1 mg enoxaparin; 8–12 h: 0.5 mg per 1 mg (unstructured: see protamine)
notes: Neutralizes at most ~60% of anti-Xa activity (label)

monitoring: No routine monitoring; anti-Xa in renal impairment, obesity, pregnancy (institution varies)
interactions: Antiplatelets, NSAIDs, other anticoagulants increase bleeding — and neuraxial hematoma risk (label)
pregnancy: First-choice anticoagulant in pregnancy; minimal transfer to breast milk (Miller 2026)
Prophylaxis in pregnancy: fixed dose (40 mg daily or 30 mg q12h) preferred to weight-based (Miller 2026)
institutionVaries: LP/neuraxial holds: see periprocedural-holds-lp-evd (ASRA 2025); label intervals are for surgery
pearls: Boxed warning: spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture — weigh before LP; risk up with indwelling catheters, NSAIDs/antiplatelets, traumatic or repeated punctures
Contraindicated with history of immune-mediated HIT within the past 100 days or circulating antibodies (label)
sources: Lovenox (enoxaparin sodium) US prescribing information. Sanofi; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)
